reason: Neither conversation recognised that a 12-year-old Hotpoint TCM580GUK sits in the Hotpoint/Indesit/Creda fire-risk recall programme, so both missed the decisive safety stop and manufacturer safety-line escalation. Conversation 2 at least answered the homeowner's repeated worry: it named the hot cabinet as a fire risk, told them explicitly not to run it while out, respected their refusal to open panels and escalated to a professional. Conversation 1 ignored the direct safety question three times, kept cycling through generic checks (including a wrong 'heat-pump' reference and sensor strips the customer couldn't find), never told them to stop running it unattended, and ended on an irrelevant question about the stop pattern. Conversation 2's wrong 'rear vent hose' instruction for a condenser model is a flaw, but its handling of the unattended-use risk makes it clearly the better service.
